applicability: Applies to expressions given as an ordered list of integer operands and a list of binary operators (+,-,*) with exactly len(operands)-1 operators, where parentheses may be inserted freely without reordering operands or operators. Returns the number of distinct integer values over all full parenthesizations. Limited to the schema bounds (1 to 8 operands, operands in [-10,20]); does not handle other operators, non-integer operands, or reordering.
description: Interval dynamic programming over sets of achievable integer values. For each contiguous subexpression a[i..j], dp[i][j] is the set of all values obtainable by fully parenthesizing it. Base case dp[i][i]={a[i]}. For longer intervals, every split point k combines each value from the left interval with each value from the right interval using the operator at position k, inserting results into a set to deduplicate. The answer is the cardinality of dp[0][n-1]. Inputs are validated against the schema (operand count 1..8, integer operands in [-10,20], operators in {+,-,*}, exactly n-1 operators); malformed inputs raise ValueError. The computation is exact and deterministic. Uncertainty: worst-case value sets can grow quickly, but the bounded input size keeps it feasible; no semantic ambiguity remains.
